diagnostic_evidence.quote: and assume that $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{A}(\mathbb{I}_1,\mathbb{I}_2)$ has the maximal volume among all $S_1\times S_2$ submatrices of $\mathbf{A}$
enhancing the theory behind the adaptive sampling strategies

issues.failure_explanation: The only CUR error bound (Theorem 4.1 / Corollary 4.2) assumes the core is the maximal-volume submatrix of the full coefficient matrix A. That selection needs all of A, which the paper says is unavailable in practice. Algorithms 1 and 2 pick nested blocks of low-frequency indices and stop on a heuristic sigma_min/Frobenius ratio, so no bound covers them. The conclusion's future-work item about enhancing the theory of the adaptive strategies concedes this. The abstract nonetheless asserts rigorous bounds for both proposed strategies.

failure_location.quote: Theoretical error bounds are derived for both approaches, ensuring rigorous control over approximation quality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract and conclusion: bounds hold only for maximal-volume index selection (and, given the next issues, in a corrected form). Present Algorithms 1 and 2 as heuristics without error guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The paper gives no guarantee that the output of Algorithm 1 or 2 approximates Ff within any tolerance. The advertised 'rigorous control over approximation quality' holds only for an idealised maximal-volume choice that the algorithms do not implement.
issues.title: Abstract claims error bounds for both strategies; bounds exist only for an (unattainable) maximal-volume selection
issues.why_classification: The repair is a scope rewording, but the advertised guarantee for the actual algorithms is lost and would need new analysis to restore.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for the approximation of multivariate functions under certain conditions

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that for any f in L^2([a,b]^2), taking I_n >= (1/eps)^{1/alpha} gives error <= sqrt(2) eps. It states no smoothness or singular-value-decay hypothesis, and alpha is not tied to any assumption on f. The truncation error of the SVD/Karhunen-Loeve expansion is a tail sum of squared singular values. For a general L^2 function this can decay arbitrarily slowly, so no rate in terms of an unspecified alpha can hold. The paper itself says the cited result holds 'under certain conditions'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis (e.g. a smoothness or singular-value decay condition defining alpha) as in the cited theorem, or delete the sentence.
issues.overall_effect: The remark misstates a cited result. It is not used in the proofs or algorithms, so the damage is limited to the context it provides.
issues.title: Remark attributes to Griebel-Harbrecht a rate for arbitrary L^2 functions with undefined alpha
issues.why_classification: Adding the omitted hypothesis is a local fix, and nothing downstream depends on the remark.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof says it combines Theorem 3.1 with Theorem 3.2, but Theorem 3.1 yields min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}. The max version is strictly stronger when I_1 != I_2 and is false. Take f = exp(i k_2 x_2) with |k_2| = I_2+1 and I_1 -> infinity. Then Ff = 0, A = 0, tilde-F f = 0, and the error is 1. The claimed bound is C I_1^{-alpha}(I_2+1)^alpha, which tends to 0. Corollary 4.2 repeats the same incorrect exponent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace max by min in Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 4.2.
issues.overall_effect: Both the theorem and the corollary are false as stated for I_1 != I_2. They remain true when I_1 = I_2, which is the only case used in the experiments.
issues.title: Truncation error stated with max{I_1,I_2} although Theorem 3.1 gives only min{I_1,I_2}
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction forced by Theorem 3.1 preserves every claim actually used.

issues.failure_explanation: By Parseval, the L^2 norm of tilde-Ff - Ff equals the Frobenius norm of A - EF^*, which is the root of a sum of squares over (2I_1+1)(2I_2+1) entries. It is not bounded by the largest entry. The correct relation is ||.||_F <= sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) ||.||_max, and the inequality as written fails in general. Theorem 3.2 controls only the max norm, so the bound eps||A||_2 in the theorem does not follow. Corollary 4.2 has the same problem because Theorem 4.1 is also a max-norm bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with the factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) on the second term. This weakens the bound severely, so a meaningful result would need a Frobenius-norm low-rank bound (e.g. via singular-value tails), which is a new argument.
issues.overall_effect: The central error guarantee linking the low-rank coefficient approximation to the function-space error is unsupported. With the correct factor, eps must shrink by sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)). The rank bound R then grows by the factor (2I_1+1)(2I_2+1) and exceeds the matrix dimensions, so it becomes vacuous. The same applies to the CUR bound in Corollary 4.2.
issues.title: L^2 error bounded by max-norm of the coefficient error; it is the Frobenius norm
issues.why_classification: The only valid repair either makes the rank guarantee vacuous or needs a new Frobenius-type theory. The central eps-control guarantee is materially worse.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and the maximum number of iterations $K$
if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d)

issues.failure_explanation: The loop runs while tol>tau OR k<=K, so it ends only when both tol<=tau and k>K. K therefore cannot act as a maximum iteration count, and the loop never ends if tol stays above tau. The prose rule also differs from the pseudocode. The text continues while max{sigma_min(C)^2/nF_C, sigma_min(R)^2/nF_R} >= tau^2, i.e. it stops only when both ratios are small. The pseudocode tracks the minimum of the ratios and stops as soon as either is <= tau. These rules give different outputs. The pseudocode also starts at k=0, and the first pass then re-selects index 0 and indices +-1..+-(b_n-1). Repeated columns would give sigma_min=0. The same 'or' loop appears in Algorithm 2 and in the appendix algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use 'and' in the loop condition, fix a single stopping rule for Algorithm 1, and start the loop at k=1.
issues.overall_effect: The stated iteration bound, the resulting S_n = 2Kb_n+1 used in the cost counts, and the stopping behaviour of the algorithms are not well defined.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 (and 2, C.1) termination logic: 'or' loop condition and inconsistent stopping rules
issues.why_classification: Local, routine corrections to the control flow and indexing fix the procedure without changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: From the block sizes, iteration k evaluates 2b_2(2(k-1)b_1+1) + 2b_1(2(k-1)b_2+1) + 4b_1b_2 = 4(2k-1)b_1b_2 + 2(b_1+b_2) integrals. The paper's 4(k^2-1)b_1b_2 + 2(b_1+b_2) differs; at k=1 it gives 2(b_1+b_2) instead of 4b_1b_2 + 2(b_1+b_2). The correct count sums with the initial entry to (2Kb_1+1)(2Kb_2+1) = S_1S_2. The paper's formula does not. It is also inconsistent with the paper's own operation count, which corresponds to the correct number of entries.
issues.overall_effect: The step-by-step cost accounting for Algorithm 2 is incorrect. The final total (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2 is still correct and does not use this formula.
issues.title: Wrong per-iteration integral count for Algorithm 2
issues.why_classification: A local arithmetic correction; the conclusions of the cost analysis are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When we set $\mathbf{G}_{1k}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{2k}$ as the zero matrix
the number of double integrals in Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg1:app-main} is less than Algorithms \ref{t-lasso:alg1-main} and \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main}

issues.failure_explanation: The core G has zero off-diagonal blocks, so it is not the intersection A(I_1,I_2) = C(I_1,:) = R(:,I_2) required for a CUR/cross approximation. For exactly rank-1 A = u v^T, each diagonal block G_k is rank-1 and satisfies v_J^T G_k^dagger u_I = 1. The block-diagonal pseudoinverse therefore gives C G^dagger R = (K+1) A (K+1 blocks), a 100K% error. The algorithm also still computes all of C and R, which contain the skipped off-diagonal blocks of the core. The distinct integrals needed are (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2, the same as Algorithm 2. The claimed count with -2S_1S_2+Kb_1b_2 is below the size of the union of C and R, so it is impossible. The diagonal blocks also contain 4Kb_1b_2+1 entries, not Kb_1b_2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the true core G = A(I_1,I_2) (i.e. Algorithm 2) and withdraw the claimed integral savings, or derive a justified block-diagonal variant with a correct count.
issues.overall_effect: The modified algorithm does not produce a valid CUR approximation, even for rank-1 coefficient matrices. Its claimed saving in integrals is false, and the appendix numerical comparison cannot support its validity.
issues.title: Appendix 'modified' algorithm uses a block-diagonal core and a miscounted integral saving
issues.why_classification: The repair is to revert to the existing Algorithm 2 construction. The claimed savings of the variant are lost, but the main algorithms are unaffected.
